Information about the requestor's vessel, including a description of the proposed service, is in the SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION section below.","publishedAt":"2026-11-06","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22678","title":"Notice of Intent of Waiver With Respect to Land; Watertown Regional Airport, Watertown, South Dakota","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/06/2026-22678/notice-of-intent-of-waiver-with-respect-to-land-watertown-regional-airport-watertown-south-dakota","summary":"The FAA is considering a proposal to change approximately 4.99 acres of airport land from aeronautical use to non-aeronautical use and to authorize the sale of airport property located at the Watertown Regional Airport, Watertown, SD. The aforementioned land is not needed for aeronautical use. The subject property is made up of two parcels of airport property known as the Lot 4 (2.0 acres) and Dakota Tube (2.99 acres) parcels. These parcels are located north of the airport, along the east side of Airport Drive. Both properties are currently being used for industrial purposes and will continue to be used for the same purpose in the future.","publishedAt":"2026-11-06","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22667","title":"Establishment of Class E Airspace, Shelter Cove Airport, Shelter Cove, CA","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/06/2026-22667/establishment-of-class-e-airspace-shelter-cove-airport-shelter-cove-ca","summary":"This action proposes to establish a Class E airspace area extending upwards from 700 feet above the surface of the earth at Shelter Cove Airport (K0Q5), Shelter Cove, CA. K0Q5 is transitioning from a visual flight rules (VFR) to an instrument flight rules (IFR) airport. Additionally, this action would establish a controlled airspace area for the airport, providing coverage to arriving IFR aircraft descending below 1,500 feet above the surface and departing IFR aircraft until reaching 1,200 feet above the surface.","publishedAt":"2026-11-06","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22665","title":"Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/06/2026-22665/airworthiness-directives-airbus-sas-airplanes","summary":"The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-19-03, which applies to certain Airbus SAS Model A350-941 and - 1041 airplanes. AD 2024-19-03 requires revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-19-03, the FAA has determined that new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations are necessary. This proposed AD would continue to require certain actions in AD 2024-19-03 and would require revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-06","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22664","title":"Airworthiness Directives; Dassault Aviation Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/06/2026-22664/airworthiness-directives-dassault-aviation-airplanes","summary":"The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-15-04, which applies to certain Dassault Aviation Model FALCON 7X airplanes. AD 2024-15-04 requires revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-15- 04, the FAA has determined that new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations are necessary. This proposed AD would continue to require certain actions in AD 2024-15-04 and would require revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-06","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22651","title":"Deadline for Submitting Intent To Use Airport Improvement Program (AIP) Apportioned Funds for Fiscal Year (FY) 2027","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/06/2026-22651/deadline-for-submitting-intent-to-use-airport-improvement-program-aip-apportioned-funds-for-fiscal","summary":"Title 49 U.S.C. 47105(f) provides that every sponsor of an airport for which AIP funds are apportioned shall notify the Secretary, by such time and in a form prescribed by the Secretary, of its intent to submit a grant application for its available entitlement funds. This notice establishes the annual national deadline and requirements for every airport sponsor to signal their intent to submit applications for FY 2027 AIP entitlement funds. This is necessary to ensure the FAA has sufficient time to convert and carry over (protect) undeclared apportionment funds.","publishedAt":"2026-11-06","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22642","title":"Modification of Class D and Class E Airspace Areas; Roberts Field/Redmond Municipal Airport, Redmond, OR","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/05/2026-22642/modification-of-class-d-and-class-e-airspace-areas-roberts-fieldredmond-municipal-airport-redmond-or","summary":"This action modifies the Class D and Class E airspace areas designated as a surface area, the Class E airspace area designated as an extension to a Class D or Class E surface area, and the Class E airspace area extending upward from 700 feet above the surface at Roberts Field/Redmond Municipal Airport, Redmond, OR. This action supports the safety and management of visual flight rules (VFR) and instrument flight rules (IFR) operations at the airport.","publishedAt":"2026-11-05","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22617","title":"Deepwater Port Application Processing and Licensing","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/05/2026-22617/deepwater-port-application-processing-and-licensing","summary":"This document proposes procedures for the processing of applications for the licensing of deepwater ports. The proposed rule reflects the transfer of deepwater port license application processing management under the Deepwater Port Act from the United States Coast Guard (USCG) to MARAD. Pursuant to the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 (2026 NDAA), MARAD is the Federal lead agency for purposes of the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (NEPA) for all deepwater port license applications. USCG responsibility for authorities pertaining to design, construction, equipment, operation of deepwater ports, and navigational safety are not affected by the 2026 NDAA statutory changes, or this proposed rule and will continue to be administered by USCG.","publishedAt":"2026-11-05","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22591","title":"Agency Information Collection Activities: Notice of Request for Renewal of Currently Approved Information Collection","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/05/2026-22591/agency-information-collection-activities-notice-of-request-for-renewal-of-currently-approved","summary":"The FHWA invites public comments about our intention to request the Office of Management and Budget's (OMB) approval for renewal of an existing information collection that is summarized below under SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION. We are required to publish this notice in the Federal Register by the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995.","publishedAt":"2026-11-05","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22587","title":"Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/05/2026-22587/airworthiness-directives-airbus-sas-airplanes","summary":"The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus SAS Model A318-111 and -112 airplanes; Model A319- 111, -112, -113, -114, -115, -131, -132, and -133 airplanes; Model A320-211, -212, -214, -216, -231, -232, and -233 airplanes; and Model A321-111, -112, -131, -211, -212, -213, -231, and -232 airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by reports of damage to the YZ-axis attachment points on airplanes equipped with certain overhead stowage compartments (OHSC) bins. Investigations showed that bushings, retainer rings, and pins had migrated from their original positions. This proposed AD would require a one-time inspection for discrepancies of affected OHSC bins and, depending on findings, accomplishment of applicable corrective actions. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected parts. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-05","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22586","title":"Agency Information Collection Activities: Notice of Request for Renewal of a Currently Approved Information Collection.","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/05/2026-22586/agency-information-collection-activities-notice-of-request-for-renewal-of-a-currently-approved","summary":"The FHWA has forwarded the information collection request described in this notice to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for the renewal of an existing information collection. We are required to publish this notice in the Federal Register by the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995.","publishedAt":"2026-11-05","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22564","title":"Airworthiness Directives; Costruzioni Aeronautiche Tecnam S.P.A. Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/05/2026-22564/airworthiness-directives-costruzioni-aeronautiche-tecnam-spa-airplanes","summary":"The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Costruzioni Aeronautiche Tecnam S.P.A. (Tecnam) Model P2006T airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a report of damage on the engine mount structure caused by defective non-conforming engine shock mounts being installed. This proposed AD would require inspecting for the installation of non-conforming engine shock mounts and replacing any non-conforming engine shock mount with an approved part. This proposed AD would also prohibit installation of a non-conforming engine shock mount on any airplane. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-05","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22512","title":"Parts and Accessories Necessary for Safe Operation; Metronet Application for Exemption","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/04/2026-22512/parts-and-accessories-necessary-for-safe-operation-metronet-application-for-exemption","summary":"FMCSA requests public comment on an application from Metronet for an exemption from the requirement that all exterior lighting devices be steady burning. The exemption would allow Metronet to use Grote Industries LLC's (Grote) amber brake-activated pulsating lamp on its commercial motor vehicles (CMVs), including pickup truck service vehicles not covered by the exemption FMCSA previously granted to Grote, in addition to the steady-burning brake lamps required by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations (FMCSRs).","publishedAt":"2026-11-04","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22510","title":"Qualification of Drivers; Exemption Applications; Epilepsy and Seizure Disorders","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/04/2026-22510/qualification-of-drivers-exemption-applications-epilepsy-and-seizure-disorders","summary":"FMCSA announces its decision to exempt 16 individuals from the requirement in the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations (FMCSRs) that interstate commercial motor vehicle (CMV) drivers have \"no established medical history or clinical diagnosis of epilepsy or any other condition which is likely to cause loss of consciousness or any loss of ability to control a CMV.\" The exemptions enable these individuals who have had one or more seizures and are taking anti- seizure medication to operate CMVs in interstate commerce.","publishedAt":"2026-11-04","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-22508","title":"Qualification of Drivers; Eastern United States","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/04/2026-22497/amendment-of-domestic-very-high-frequency-omnidirectional-range-vor-federal-airways-v-16-v-35-v-37","summary":"This action corrects a final rule published by the FAA in the Federal Register on October 14, 2026, amending domestic Very High Frequency Omnidirectional Range (VOR) Federal Airways V-16, V-35, V-37, V-53, V-133, V-136, V-143, V-259, V-310, V-364, V-409, V-415, V-454, and V-605. Specifically, this action administratively corrects an error in the preamble of the rule within the description of V-37.","publishedAt":"2026-11-04","source":"Federal Register"}]}
